We are using the identity

$$
{tan}^{2}⁡x+1={sec}^{2}⁡x\,⟹\,{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1.
$$

Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}\frac{3(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}\frac{({sec}^{2}⁡x-1)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\operatorname{sec}⁡x\,{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3} \\  & =3\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-3\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =3\cdot 2-3\cdot \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =6-2\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
